finding.title: auth_exceptions_test.dart locks in inconsistent PII redaction between sibling exception types
finding.rule: EH-5 (stable codes, not pre-formatted messages) / privacy consistency
finding.why: The same test file proves the codebase knows raw emails shouldn't land in an exception's toString() — DuplicateEmailException's docstring (local_auth_service.dart:11-13) says so explicitly and this file asserts it (line 18) — yet asserts the opposite for EmailCollisionException (line 71), whose message is built as '$email is already in use' (upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart:12). The 3 current catch sites in upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart only branch on the exception's type today, but EH-1's global FlutterError.onError/PlatformDispatcher.onError handler forwards uncaught exceptions to AppLogger, typically by serializing toString(); if EmailCollisionException ever escapes a catch clause (new call site, refactor) the plaintext email reaches the logger/Crashlytics pipeline with nothing to stop it, unlike its sibling.
finding.recommendation: Give EmailCollisionException the same email/redactedEmail split as DuplicateEmailException (keep the field, drop the raw address from message/toString), and update this test's assertion accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: EmailCollisionException.toString() no longer contains the raw email; a redactedEmail (or equivalent) accessor exists for callers that need a log-safe form
auth_exceptions_test.dart's EmailCollisionException group asserts the same log-safety property as the DuplicateEmailException group

finding.title: Populate content_browsing.dart barrel with real exports so Rule 2 has a legal import path
finding.why: The barrel file has zero export statements, so there is no compliant way for other code to reach ContentRepository, contentRepositoryProvider, curriculumContentProvider or ContentItemTile — every consumer (core/labels/, core/content/, and every deep import inside this batch's own screens into dashboard/learning/scheduler/tutoring/gamification/tracks) is forced into a deep import because the barrel offers nothing. lib/features/progress/progress.dart shows the intended pattern (documented policy + real `export` lines); content_browsing's barrel (like several other features sampled: gamification, dashboard, onboarding, notifications, profiles, learning) is only a decorative stub.
finding.recommendation: Follow progress.dart's pattern: export ContentRepository, contentRepositoryProvider, curriculumContentProvider, and ContentItemTile with a comment naming each external consumer, then migrate at least the deep imports inside this batch to the barrel.
acceptance_criteria: content_browsing.dart contains one or more `export` statements for types already consumed outside the feature
flutter analyze stays clean after switching at least one external consumer (e.g. core/labels/curriculum_label_providers.dart) to the barrel import

finding.title: Fix Makefile check-15 cross-feature-import grep — its awk logic can never report a violation

evidence.quote: match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print

finding.why: match($0, ...) scans the WHOLE grep -n output line (path:line:content), so it finds the importing file's own 'features/content_browsing/' path segment before it ever reaches the import statement's 'features/dashboard/' target — a[1] and b[1] are therefore always equal and the WARN block never fires, for any input. Reproduced live: piping content_hierarchy_screen.dart's real dashboard_providers.dart import through this exact awk yields a[1]=content_browsing b[1]=content_browsing. make audit prints '15/15 ... PASSED — all 22 greps clean', but this batch alone has 10+ genuine deep cross-feature imports (content_hierarchy_screen.dart:18, content_search_screen.dart:16, curriculum_list_screen.dart:14, text_display_screen.dart:24/28-36, content_item_tile.dart:11-13, hierarchy_selection_panel.dart:14) that check 15 was supposed to at least warn about and silently does not, unlike check 14 (core→features) which works correctly and lists 32 real edges.
finding.recommendation: Fix the awk to extract the feature name from the import statement only, e.g. strip the 'path:line:' prefix before matching, or match against 'import .*features/([^/]+)/' specifically instead of generic $0.
acceptance_criteria: a fixture line containing a genuine cross-feature deep import, piped through the fixed check, produces non-empty WARN output
make audit re-run after the fix lists real cross-feature deep imports (e.g. this batch's dashboard_providers.dart imports) as new WARN entries

finding.title: Remove dead cloud-content-download and text-download-status code paths

evidence.quote: Future<bool> isTextDownloaded(Ref ref, CurriculumId curriculumId) async {
/// @deprecated — Text content is now bundled in the seed database.

finding.why: grep -rn across lib/ confirms cloudContentServiceProvider, contentDownloadStatusDaoProvider, and isTextDownloadedProvider have no watchers/readers anywhere outside their own definition files — cloudContentService's own doc comment admits it is 'Retained for potential future use'. This keeps ~450 lines alive (the full 359-line cloud_content_service.dart plus the 66-line text_download_service.dart) including a duplicate download-state/progress modeling pattern (ContentDownloadState/Progress vs TextDownloadState/Progress are near-identical), and wires a real FirebaseStorage dependency via firebaseStorageProvider for a path nothing exercises. The '@deprecated' marker on downloadCurriculum is a doc comment, not a real @Deprecated() annotation, so the analyzer cannot warn a future caller either.
finding.recommendation: Delete cloud_content_service.dart, cloud_content_providers.dart, text_download_service.dart, and the textDownloadService/isTextDownloaded providers, or if a near-term roadmap need is real, replace the speculative comment with a Linear ticket id per AG-6 and wire one actual caller.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn for cloudContentServiceProvider/contentDownloadStatusDaoProvider/isTextDownloadedProvider in lib/ returns no hits (or a real non-self caller)
flutter analyze stays clean; the corresponding now-orphaned test files (cloud_content_service_test.dart, text_download_service_test.dart) are removed or updated in the same change
